scenarios.task: Issue #482 reports that parse_csv() silently drops the last field when the input file uses CRLF line endings. Confirm the bug and fix it, following a test-first regression workflow.
scenarios.fixture: A small Python library where parse_csv() splits rows on '\n', which mishandles CRLF-terminated files (the trailing '\r' corrupts the last field and the final row's last field is dropped). tests/test_parser.py exists and is fully green; there is no test covering CRLF-only input.

rubric.criterion: Wrote the regression test before applying any fix, and confirmed it failed for the actual bug (not a setup error) before touching source code
Test name/description references the specific scenario (CRLF-only input) or issue #482, not a generic name like test_bug
Applied the smallest fix to the line-ending handling without bundling unrelated refactors of parse_csv into the same change
Ran the new test plus the surrounding suite after the fix and both passed
Did not assert on incidental implementation details (e.g. internal buffer state) beyond the observable parsing behavior

scenarios.task: Fix the bulk-discount bug in the billing calculator: customers ordering exactly 10 units should get the discount but currently don't. It's a single-character fix, but ship it with proper regression coverage.
scenarios.fixture: billing/discount.py contains `if quantity > 10:` where the documented threshold is inclusive, so it should be `>= 10`. tests/test_discount.py exists with several unrelated passing tests; none of them cover quantity == 10.

rubric.criterion: Did not skip writing a regression test on the grounds that the fix is a single-character change
Wrote the test first, ran it, and confirmed it failed before applying the one-line fix
New test was placed in tests/test_discount.py alongside the existing tests, matching their style and fixtures
Fix touched only the discount source file and its test file, with no unrelated files modified

scenarios.task: Users report that exporting a report to PDF produces a blank first page. Diagnose the actual defect and fix it with a proper regression test, rather than patching around the visible symptom.
scenarios.fixture: report_export.py renders pages from a list of page objects. The root cause is an off-by-one in one branch's bounds check (the page loop starts at index 1 instead of 0), which happens to manifest as a blank first page for single-page reports. tests/test_export.py is currently green because no test exercises single-page reports.

rubric.criterion: Diagnosed the actual root cause (the off-by-one index bug) rather than patching around the visible symptom, e.g. by special-casing or re-inserting a page
The regression test's failure message, observed before the fix, reflects the real bug (wrong page rendered/skipped) rather than a generic assertion
The fix changes the index bounds logic itself, not a superficial workaround layered on top of it
Ran the new test plus the full surrounding suite after the fix and confirmed both green
